title: Hardik Pandya Must Pass a Fitness Test Before He Can Play the Afghanistan ODIs. Rohit Hasn't Reported to the NCA Either.
excerpt: The BCCI's Centre of Excellence clearance is mandatory for both all-rounder and former captain, leaving India's ODI squad in flux before the three-match series begins on June 13
body:
Hardik Pandya has been named in India's 15-member squad for the three-match ODI series against Afghanistan, but there is a significant caveat: the all-rounder must obtain fitness clearance from the BCCI's Centre of Excellence before he can be considered for selection.

The demand reflects a broader pattern within Indian cricket's new management structure, where fitness benchmarks are no longer discretionary. Pandya, who had a gruelling IPL 2026 campaign with Mumbai Indians, has been dealing with workload management concerns that have followed him since his back surgery in 2019.

## The Fitness Question

Chief selector Ajit Agarkar confirmed that Pandya's inclusion is conditional. "We've named him in the squad, but he needs to report to the Centre of Excellence and pass the fitness tests," Agarkar told reporters. "That's non-negotiable for anyone who's been managing a workload issue."

Pandya is not the only senior player whose participation remains uncertain. Rohit Sharma, who was also named in the ODI squad, has yet to report to the Centre of Excellence. Reports suggest the former captain prefers to train independently in Mohali rather than at the NCA in Bangalore, creating an awkward situation for the team management.

## A Packed ODI Schedule

The three ODIs against Afghanistan — in Dharamsala on June 13, Lucknow on June 17, and Chennai on June 20 — represent the beginning of a dense white-ball schedule for India. The series is being treated as crucial preparation for the 2027 ODI World Cup in Africa, and the selectors want to assess combinations that might serve India in the longer run.

The squad already has significant gaps. Virat Kohli has been ruled out with a hamstring injury sustained during RCB's title-winning IPL 2026 final. Yashasvi Jaiswal has replaced him, a move that signals the selectors' willingness to give younger players opportunities in the middle order.

Jasprit Bumrah has been rested from both the Test and ODI squads as part of workload management — a decision that has become routine for India's most valuable fast bowler.

## What Pandya Brings

When fit, Pandya remains India's only genuine pace-bowling all-rounder at the international level. His ability to bowl four to six overs of pace and bat in the lower middle order gives the team a balance that no other player in the squad can replicate. Nitish Kumar Reddy offers a similar profile but is still developing his international credentials.

The concern is durability. Pandya's history of back and shoulder injuries has made every selection a calculated risk. The BCCI's insistence on fitness clearance is as much about protecting the player as it is about ensuring India do not lose a key player mid-series to a breakdown.

## The Diaspora Angle

For NRI fans planning to follow the series, the uncertainty around Pandya and Rohit makes the squad composition a moving target. The Dharamsala opener is particularly appealing for cricket-loving diaspora members visiting the hill station, but whether they will see a full-strength India remains unclear until the fitness reports are filed.

Ishan Kishan's return to the squad after nearly three years adds another storyline. The wicketkeeper-batter, whose last ODI was against Afghanistan in early 2024, has been named alongside KL Rahul, giving India two keeping options and raising questions about the batting order configuration.

India's ODI squad: Shubman Gill (c), Rohit Sharma*, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Shreyas Iyer (vc), KL Rahul (wk), Ishan Kishan (wk), Hardik Pandya*, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Washington Sundar, Kuldeep Yadav, Arshdeep Singh, Prasidh Krishna, Prince Yadav, Gurnoor Brar, Harsh Dubey. (*Subject to fitness clearance)
